newsitem.title: USA: PBS forms business-education joint venture.
newsitem.headline: PBS forms business-education joint venture.

text.p: The Public Broadcasting Service said on Tuesday it had formed a joint venture with an unnamed U.S company to electronically deliver to businesses educational programs, seminars and interactive services.
A spokeswoman for PBS declined to identify the company or provide details beyond announcement of a news conference scheduled here at 1015 ET on Thursday.

PBS President Ervin Duggan and the chief executive officer of an unidentified Fortune 500 company will be among the presenters. Writer and Massachusetts of Technology professor Lester Thurow will also appear at the news conference.
Sun Microsystems, whose chief executive Scott McNealy is to speak in New York on Thursday, is to provide some technology to the venture, an industry source said.

The source said the joint venture, just the latest profit-making initiative by public televison groups seeking to replace dwindling government funding, would use high-capacity fiber optic lines to deliver the services to personal computers and would tap PBS' big library of educational films.
The venture would have on-demand video services, as well as lectures. Such topics as changing government regulations and foreign languages would be offered, the source said.
